description: Source-lore pass 8 imports water scarcity, rain and cloud-dew harvesting, mundane and magical storage, water transport, and the political economy of freshwater in the skies.

entries.title: Water in the Skies of Kaysender
entries.summary: Fresh water is a constant survival problem in Kaysender because open skies and many floating islands lack dependable rivers, lakes, rainfall, and accessible springs.
body: Water is one of the defining constraints of life in Kaysender. The aerial world is filled with [[floating-islands|floating islands]], skyships, and immense open distances, but reliable fresh water is scarce. Air sailors, traders, adventurers, settlements, and entire fleets must plan around obtaining, carrying, protecting, and rationing it.

The lands far below may hold rivers, lakes, and oceans, but the sky itself does not. Many floating islands are arid or sparsely vegetated and cannot support large bodies of water. The rare waterfalls, streams, and springs may lie deep beneath jungle canopies or inside difficult mountain interiors, making discovery and access uncertain.

Open-sky travel offers little natural relief. Rain is brief and unpredictable, and cloud layers do not automatically yield usable water. Crews that leave port without dependable reserves risk thirst long before they reach another island, especially when storms, route changes, or damaged equipment extend a voyage.

This scarcity connects water directly to [[grim-realities-of-survival|the grim realities of survival]]. Every settlement and vessel must balance crew size, journey length, cargo weight, collection equipment, storage capacity, contamination risk, and access to [[water-trade|water markets]].

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Water in the Skies of Kaysender

entries.title: Rain and Cloud-Dew Harvesting
entries.summary: Skyships and settlements gather water through unreliable rain-catching apparatus and specialized cloud-dew collection, both constrained by weather, time, equipment, and contamination.
body: Some skyships carry rain-catching apparatus, but these systems depend on meeting a storm at the right place and time. A passing shower may provide useful water, yet the amount is often too small for a large crew or a long voyage.

Storm harvesting carries its own danger. Violent weather threatens rigging, crew, cargo, and the vessel itself, while captured rain may be contaminated or spoil in storage. A desperate crew must decide whether the promise of water justifies entering dangerous skies.

Several cultures also gather cloud dew by condensing moisture from cloud layers. This process requires specialized tools, magic, preparation, and time. It can supplement reserves, but it is not dependable enough to replace planned storage and resupply.

Rain catchers and cloud-dew collectors therefore function as survival infrastructure rather than effortless sources. Their value rises sharply in remote regions, aboard small vessels, and in settlements cut off from [[water-trade|water convoys]].

entries.title: Water Storage and Transport
entries.summary: Kaysender crews move water in heavy casks, kegs, and barrels or in costly enchanted containers that compress large reserves into portable forms.
body: Because water cannot be gathered reliably in flight, air sailors and travelers depend on stored reserves. Ordinary casks, kegs, and barrels remain the foundation of water transport, but their bulk and weight consume valuable cargo capacity and make long journeys difficult.

A small cask is intended to sustain one traveler for several days. A keg supports a small group on a short journey, while a reinforced barrel carries a much larger reserve for crews and extended travel. Kegs and barrels require multiple people, carts, or ships to move safely.

The logistical burden of mundane containers has created demand for enchanted storage. Compact flasks and waterskins can carry barrel- or keg-sized reserves at a fraction of the weight. These items are prized aboard airships and on expeditions but remain too expensive for many common travelers and crews.

Storage is inseparable from [[cargo-standards|cargo planning]] and [[water-trade|water supply routes]]. Every container devoted to water displaces profitable freight, food, passengers, or equipment, but insufficient reserves can destroy a voyage or settlement.

sections.heading: Legacy Container Measures
body: The source lists a 10 gp cask holding 3 gallons and sustaining one person for approximately 3 days; a 30 gp keg holding 10 gallons and sustaining up to four people for 7 days; and a 50 gp barrel holding 40 gallons and sustaining four people for 14 days.

The source describes a cask as person-portable, a keg as a two-person load or cart cargo, and a barrel as requiring two or three people or ship or wagon transport. These prices, capacities, and consumption rates are preserved for later rules conversion.

entries.title: Water Trade
entries.summary: Fresh water is a luxury commodity, settlement lifeline, strategic cargo, and political weapon whose sources and routes shape trade, rivalry, and survival throughout Kaysender.
body: The difficulty of acquiring and carrying water has created dedicated supply routes between freshwater sources, floating cities, skyports, and thirsty settlements. Merchant fleets transport barrels and enchanted reserves across the skies and charge high prices because loss, spoilage, piracy, weather, and cargo weight make every shipment risky.

The source associates this trade with organizations such as [[whisper-web|the Whisper Web]] and [[skyweaver-consortium|the Skyweaver Consortium]]. Their access to routes, information, ships, and storage gives merchant organizations enormous influence over communities that cannot secure their own water.

Some islands and floating cities build their economies around collection and distribution. A rare freshwater spring, stream, reservoir, or dependable rain corridor can turn an otherwise minor island into a wealthy trade center. Communities without access must buy, ration, bargain, or fight for supply.

Control of freshwater is therefore political power. Rival factions compete for sources and transport corridors; settlements become vulnerable when cisterns fail or convoys are delayed; and adventurers must plan every journey around reserves, resupply, and the possibility that promised water will be unavailable, contaminated, or unaffordable.

Water trade links [[grim-realities-of-survival|daily survival]] to markets, diplomacy, piracy, tribute, and war. It shapes settlement resilience, fleet endurance, migration, route planning, and the balance between independent communities and the organizations that keep them alive.

entries.title: Arcane Flask of Water
entries.summary: An Arcane Flask of Water is a compact leather-bound enchanted vessel that carries a barrel-sized reserve while remaining light enough for a backpack.
body: An Arcane Flask of Water looks like a simple, sleek, leather-bound container, but its enchantment gives it the capacity of a full water barrel. It is compact enough for a backpack and provides fresh, clean water when opened.

The flask is valuable because it replaces a large, heavy barrel with a portable container. For airship crews and expeditions, that reduction in weight and cargo volume can be as important as the water itself.

Arcane flasks still belong to the economy of scarcity. Their high price keeps them beyond many travelers, while their usefulness makes them valuable cargo and likely targets for theft, salvage, or seizure during a supply crisis.

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Notes
body: The source prices the flask at 150 gp, gives it a 40-gallon capacity, describes it as sufficient for four people for 14 days, permits drawing one gallon per action, states that it refills after 24 hours, and gives it a weight of 5 pounds.
These values and the refill behavior are preserved as legacy source mechanics and require conversion before use as final Hypertext d20-compatible rules.

entries.title: Feyborne Waterskin
entries.summary: A Feyborne Waterskin is a radiant, embroidered canteen crafted by fey artisans to hold a keg-sized water reserve in a small and lightweight vessel.
body: Crafted by [[fae|fey artisans]], a Feyborne Waterskin appears no larger than an ordinary canteen. Its delicate shimmering fabric and embroidered designs glow faintly with natural energy, while enchantment expands its interior capacity.

The waterskin carries the equivalent of a keg without the keg's bulk. It is especially useful to small parties and airship crews that need meaningful reserves but cannot surrender much cargo space or assign multiple people to moving a container.

Like other enchanted water vessels, the waterskin is a costly answer to a universal need. Its craftsmanship ties survival equipment to fey trade and makes the item a practical luxury in regions dependent on [[water-trade|imported water]].

sections.heading: Legacy Mechanics Notes
body: The source prices the waterskin at 100 gp, gives it a 10-gallon capacity, describes it as sufficient for four people for 7 days, permits drawing one gallon per action, and gives it a weight of 2 pounds.
These values are preserved as legacy source mechanics and require conversion before use as final Hypertext d20-compatible rules.
